cls: Purine nucleoside analog / selective immune reconstitution therapy (lymphocyte-depleting antineoplastic)
pharm: Chlorinated deoxyadenosine prodrug that is intracellularly phosphorylated to its active triphosphate, preferentially accumulating in and depleting B and T lymphocytes. The oral product (Mavenclad) is given as short, cumulative weight-based courses for relapsing multiple sclerosis, producing prolonged lymphocyte depletion followed by reconstitution; the parenteral product (Leustatin/Litak) is used to treat hairy cell leukemia.

No change for mild; NOT recommended in moderate-severe (Child-Pugh >6)

summary: Cladribine is a purine nucleoside analog that selectively depletes lymphocytes. The oral tablet (Mavenclad) treats relapsing forms of multiple sclerosis in adults, generally reserved for those with inadequate response or intolerance to other MS therapies, and is given as a low cumulative dose of 3.5 mg/kg over 2 years. It carries two boxed warnings - increased risk of malignancy and severe teratogenicity (contraindicated in pregnancy and in women or men of reproductive potential not using effective contraception). Key risks include marked lymphopenia, serious infections (including herpes reactivation and rare PML concern), hematologic toxicity, and liver injury, requiring screening and lymphocyte-guided dosing. The intravenous formulation (Leustatin/Litak) is used to treat hairy cell leukemia.
indications: Relapsing forms of multiple sclerosis (relapsing-remitting and active secondary progressive disease) in adults - oral Mavenclad; generally for patients with inadequate response to or intolerance of other MS drugs
Not recommended for clinically isolated syndrome because of safety profile
Hairy cell leukemia (active disease) - intravenous Leustatin/Litak

dosage.d: Cumulative 3.5 mg/kg given as 2 yearly treatment courses of 1.75 mg/kg each
dosage.t: Course 2 starts at least 43 weeks after course 1
dosage.n: No additional cladribine treatment in the 2 years following the 2 completed courses; no further treatment in years 3 and 4

dosage.c: Relapsing MS - structure of each yearly course
dosage.d: Each 1.75 mg/kg course divided into 2 treatment cycles
dosage.t: Cycle 1 then cycle 2 separated by 23-27 days (about 1 month apart)
dosage.n: Each cycle is 1-2 tablets daily over 4-5 consecutive days

dosage.c: Relapsing MS - weight-based dose per cycle (lower weights)
dosage.d: 40-<50 kg: 40 mg (4 tabs) each cycle; 50-<60 kg: 50 mg (5 tabs) each cycle; 60-<70 kg: 60 mg (6 tabs) each cycle; 70-<80 kg: 70 mg (7 tabs) each cycle
dosage.n: 10 mg tablets; split each cycle dose over the dosing days

dosage.c: Relapsing MS - weight-based dose per cycle (higher weights)
dosage.d: 80-<90 kg: 80 mg then 70 mg; 90-<100 kg: 90 mg then 80 mg; 100-<110 kg: 100 mg then 90 mg; >=110 kg: 100 mg then 100 mg (first cycle / second cycle)
dosage.n: Below 40 kg dosing has not been established

dosage.d: Lymphocyte count must be normal before course 1 and at least 800 cells/microL before course 2
dosage.n: Delay course 2 up to 6 months for recovery; if not recovered by then, do not give further cladribine

dosage.d: Refer to the specific IV product label for the cytotoxic regimen (e.g., 0.09 mg/kg/day by continuous 7-day infusion)
dosage.n: Separate oncology product; handle as a cytotoxic agent

dosage.d: Use not recommended (about 25% higher exposure predicted)
dosage.n: No adjustment needed for mild impairment (CrCl 60-89)
No adjustment needed for mild impairment

admin: Confirm normal lymphocyte count (or >=800 cells/microL before course 2) and complete required infection, hepatitis B/C, TB, and HIV screening before starting each course
Obtain a baseline MRI within 3 months before the first course
Exclude pregnancy in females of reproductive potential before each course
Swallow tablets whole with water; do not crush or chew; handle with dry hands and wipe up any contact with skin (cytotoxic drug)
On dosing days, take only the day's allotted tablets and separate from any other oral medication by at least 3 hours
Give anti-herpes prophylaxis when lymphocyte count is below 200 cells/microL
Distribute total cycle dose over the 4-5 consecutive dosing days per the weight-based table
moa: Cladribine is a deoxyadenosine analog prodrug that is taken up by lymphocytes and phosphorylated by deoxycytidine kinase to its active triphosphate (Cd-ATP), which preferentially accumulates in cells with high deoxycytidine kinase relative to deoxynucleotidase activity. The active metabolite impairs DNA synthesis and repair, leading to selective and sustained depletion of B and T lymphocytes; this immune reconstitution is thought to underlie its benefit in relapsing MS and its cytotoxic activity in hairy cell leukemia.

absolute: Pregnancy, or women/men of reproductive potential not using effective contraception (boxed warning)
Active chronic infection such as tuberculosis or hepatitis
Breastfeeding on treatment days and for 10 days after the last dose
relative: History of prior malignancy (perform individual benefit-risk assessment)
Moderate-severe renal impairment (CrCl <60 mL/min) - use not recommended
Moderate-severe hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh >6) - use not recommended
monitor: Lymphocyte count and complete blood count
Signs of infection (including herpes, TB, hepatitis reactivation)

preg: CONTRAINDICATED (Boxed warning). Cladribine caused malformations and embryolethality in animal studies and may cause fetal harm; it must not be used in pregnant women. Exclude pregnancy before each treatment course. Females of reproductive potential must use effective contraception during dosing and for 6 months after the last dose; males with female partners of reproductive potential should use contraception during dosing and for 14 weeks after the last dose. Report exposures to the pregnancy registry (1-800-283-8088 ext 5563).
lact: Contraindicated during treatment. Cladribine is present in human milk; do not breastfeed on treatment days and for 10 days after the last dose because of the potential for serious adverse reactions in the infant.
renal: No dosage adjustment for mild renal impairment (CrCl 60-89 mL/min). Use is not recommended in moderate to severe renal impairment (CrCl <60 mL/min), where cladribine exposure is predicted to rise about 25%.
hepatic: No dosage adjustment for mild hepatic impairment. Use is not recommended in moderate to severe hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh score >6). Clinically significant liver injury has occurred; check aminotransferases, alkaline phosphatase, and bilirubin before each cycle/course and discontinue if significant liver injury develops.

major: Immunosuppressive or myelosuppressive agents - concomitant use not recommended due to additive immune/marrow suppression
Interferon-beta - concomitant use not recommended; increased lymphopenia risk
Antivirals such as lamivudine and zidovudine - avoid; may interfere with intracellular phosphorylation of cladribine
moderate: Other hematotoxic drugs - monitor hematologic parameters closely
Potent BCRP (ABCG2) inhibitors (e.g., eltrombopag) - may increase oral cladribine bioavailability; avoid during the 4-5 dosing days or interrupt the inhibitor
Potent ENT1/CNT3 transport inhibitors (e.g., ritonavir, cyclosporine, nifedipine, reserpine) - may alter cladribine distribution; use with caution
minor: No clinically significant CYP-mediated interactions expected (negligible hepatic enzyme metabolism)
interactions.food: May be taken without regard to food; a high-fat meal lowers Cmax about 29% and delays Tmax but does not change overall exposure (AUC). Separate from other oral drugs by at least 3 hours on dosing days.
interactions.alcohol: No specific interaction described; moderate alcohol use as tolerated.
interactions.diagnostics: Commonly lowers lymphocyte, neutrophil, hemoglobin, and platelet counts; may raise liver enzymes. Live or live-attenuated vaccines should be avoided during and after lymphopenia until immune recovery.

serious: Serious bacterial, viral, fungal, or parasitic infections (including herpes zoster/meningoencephalitis)
rare: Progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy concern (no MS trial cases; baseline MRI advised)
Stevens-Johnson syndrome / toxic epidermal necrolysis (identified with parenteral cladribine)
Tumor lysis (with IV use in high tumor burden)
emergency: Signs of serious infection - high fever, stiff neck, confusion, or worsening neurologic symptoms
Severe or progressive neurologic deficit (possible PML)
Jaundice, dark urine, severe right-upper-quadrant pain (liver injury)
Severe skin reaction with blistering or mucosal involvement
Shortness of breath, palpitations, or new edema (cardiac failure)

monitoring: Complete blood count with differential including lymphocytes before each course, then at months 2 and 6 after starting a course; lymphocytes must be normal before course 1 and >=800 cells/microL before course 2
Screen for tuberculosis, hepatitis B and C, and HIV before starting; assess for and treat acute infection before dosing
Baseline MRI within 3 months before the first course (PML/disease assessment)
Liver enzymes, alkaline phosphatase, and bilirubin before each cycle/course
Pregnancy testing before each course in females of reproductive potential
Routine age-appropriate cancer screening per standard guidelines
Watch for herpes reactivation; give antiviral prophylaxis if lymphocytes <200 cells/microL
counsel: This medicine can increase the risk of cancer and causes serious birth defects - you must not be pregnant, and women must use reliable birth control during treatment and for 6 months after, while men must use condoms during treatment and for 14 weeks after the last dose
It lowers your immune cells, so report any fever, cough, cold sores, shingles, or signs of infection promptly, and stay up to date on recommended (non-live) vaccinations before starting
Swallow tablets whole with water with dry hands; do not crush them, and on dosing days keep them at least 3 hours apart from your other medicines
Do not breastfeed on the days you take the tablets or for 10 days afterward
Tell your doctor about yellowing of the skin or eyes, severe rash with blistering, or any new neurologic symptoms; keep all blood-test and follow-up appointments
pk: Lymphocyte nadir typically about 2-3 months after starting a course; clinical MS benefit develops over treatment courses
Tmax about 0.5 h fasted (1.5 h with a high-fat meal); oral bioavailability ~40%
Plasma terminal half-life ~1 day; intracellular active metabolites Cd-AMP ~15 h and Cd-ATP ~10 h
Prolonged lymphocyte depletion; median recovery to >=800 cells/microL about 28 weeks; sustained effect allows only 2 short courses over 2 years
Store at 20-25 C (excursions 15-30 C permitted); protect from moisture in original packaging; handle as a cytotoxic drug
pearls: Two boxed warnings: increased malignancy risk (contraindicated in current malignancy) and teratogenicity (contraindicated in pregnancy and without effective contraception)
Total exposure is just 3.5 mg/kg over 2 years (1.75 mg/kg/year) - two short yearly courses, each with two ~monthly cycles; no further cladribine in years 3-4
Dosing is lymphocyte-gated: normal count before course 1, >=800 cells/microL before course 2; delay up to 6 months for recovery
Screen for TB, hepatitis B/C, and HIV and obtain baseline MRI before starting; give anti-herpes prophylaxis if lymphocytes <200 cells/microL
Not recommended if CrCl <60 mL/min or Child-Pugh >6; the IV product (Leustatin/Litak) is a separate cytotoxic agent for hairy cell leukemia
missed: If a dose within a treatment cycle is missed, take it the next day and extend the dosing days by one - do not double up to make up a missed dose. If a dose is missed for an entire day, add the missed day to the end of that cycle. Contact the prescriber if more than one day is missed or if there is confusion about the schedule.
overdose: There is no experience with Mavenclad overdose. Expect dose-related lymphopenia and hematologic toxicity; monitor blood counts closely and watch for infection. There is no specific antidote and hemodialysis is unlikely to be effective; management is supportive and discontinuation should be considered.
